groups.title: Tablet (E72300ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Those aged 15 years and over: take 2 tablets at a time. Those aged 8 years and over but under 15 years: take 1 tablet at a time. Take it 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.
Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported; if a skin rash or another sign of hypersensitivity appears after a dose of this medicine, stop taking it at once.
Do not go above the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.
If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had it; if you have hypersensitivity to soya or peanut, or to soya-bean oil now or in the past; if you have ever had asthma when taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is an infant under 3 months of age; if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure; or if you are 30 weeks pregnant or more.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergy to a medicine; if you have liver, kidney, heart or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain or another stomach problem that lasts or comes back, or an ulcer or a bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or fat emulsions must be given to you with care, or fat overload would place you at particular risk; or if you smoke, or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with a lot of phlegm, a cough lasting or coming back for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or a persistent headache.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
Do not keep taking it over a long period.
When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
Drowsiness may occur after a dose, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.
If symptoms do not improve after 5 or 6 doses, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take it together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, anti-Parkinson medicines and the like), cough and expectorant medicines, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, travel sickness medicines, allergy medicines).
Do not take this medicine if you stopped taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) within the last 2 weeks.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are receiving other medicines such as those for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants or steroids.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are receiving barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol.
Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.

If rash or reddening, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, shock (hives, swelling and tightness of the chest immediately after a dose, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome — severe symptoms with high fever, and a rash or reddening with burn-like blisters), asthma, generalised weakness, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes), interstitial pneumonia (cough with shortness of breath, difficulty breathing and fever), symptoms of ischaemic colitis linked to the pseudoephedrine component (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding), or reversible posterior encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (a sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance and the like) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (101309ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for fever and pain caused by a cold, headache, neuralgia, muscle pain, menstrual pain, the pain of a sprain, toothache, joint pain and rheumatic pain.
groups.usage: Children aged 12 years and under: take the recommended dose for the age at a time, every 4 to 6 hours as required. Take this medicine at the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible period, and do not take it more than 5 times in 1 day (75 mg/kg). If the body weight is known, it is better to take the dose worked out from body weight (10 to 15 mg/kg). For the dose for each age group, refer to the approved product information.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.
Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported; if a skin rash or another sign of hypersensitivity appears after a dose of this medicine, stop taking it at once.
Do not go above the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, liver disorder, kidney disorder or reduced heart function, or if you have aspirin asthma (an asthma attack brought on by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicines) now or in the past.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have liver disorder or have had it, kidney disorder or have had it, a history of peptic ulcer, a blood disorder or have had one, a tendency to bleed, abnormal heart function or a history of hypersensitivity; if you have bronchial asthma; if you are an older person; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.
Without the advice of a doctor or pharmacist, do not take it for pain for 10 days or more (adults) or 5 days or more (children), and do not take it for fever for 3 days or more.

Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are taking barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol, or if you take it together with warfarin, lithium or thiazide diuretics.

If shock symptoms (difficulty breathing, reddening of the whole body, swelling of the blood vessels, hives and the like), an asthma attack, a fall in platelets, granulocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia (destruction of red cells), methaemoglobinaemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, hypersensitivity symptoms (facial swelling, difficulty breathing, sweating, low blood pressure, shock), nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, gastrointestinal effects with long-term use such as gastrointestinal bleeding, peptic ulcer or perforation, rash, an allergic reaction, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), a rise in AST, a rise in ALT or a fixed drug eruption occurs, or if pain or fever lasts or gets worse, or new symptoms appear, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Capsule (A51300ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin B6 in pregnancy and breast-feeding and when strength is reduced during or after an illness, for the relief of angular cheilitis (inflammation at the corners of the mouth), cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis, and for the prevention and treatment of iron deficiency anaemia.
groups.usage: Those aged 12 years and over and adults: take 1 capsule at a time, 1 time in 1 day, between meals.
groups.caution:
An overdose in a child aged 6 years or under can cause fatal iron poisoning, so keep it out of the reach of children.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have haemochromatosis (a disease in which iron is deposited in the liver and pancreas because of abnormal iron metabolism), haemosiderosis or anaemia that is not due to iron deficiency; or if you are short of folic acid. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional colitis, impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney disorder, or a low protein level in the blood. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline antibiotics, antacids or levodopa. Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with anti-aldosterone medicines or triamterene. Avoid tea containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, during the period of use and just before and after a dose.

If hives, itching, a photosensitivity reaction, abdominal or stomach pain, cramps, vomiting, diarrhoea, fever or coma occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (E76400ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins D, B1, B2 and B6 in physical tiredness, in pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after an illness, during growth and in later life. Through the vitamins it contains it is used for the relief of neuralgia, muscle pain, back pain, joint pain such as stiff shoulders, and angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis. Through the vitamins it contains it is also used for poor growth of the bones and teeth, the prevention of rickets, beriberi and tired eyes.
groups.usage: Those aged 8 years and over and adults: take 1 tablet at a time, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have a high calcium level in the blood, sarcoidosis, kidney disease, kidney stones or severe kidney failure; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or an infant; if the user is a child who gets plenty of sunlight and eats normally; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney disorder or a low protein level in the blood; or if you have had kidney stones.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
If you are short of folic acid, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
It can turn the urine yellow and so affect laboratory test results.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa while you are taking this medicine.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if it is taken together with anti-aldosterone medicines or triamterene.
Avoid tea containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, during the period of use and just before and after a dose.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, loose stools, stomatitis, loss of appetite, a feeling of abdominal bloating, red patches, cardiac arrest or reduced function of the central nervous system occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Supply of vitamins D, B1, B2 and B6, with relief of nerve, muscle and joint pain and mouth and skin inflammation, and support for bone and tooth growth

groups.title: Soft capsule (E23500ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of headache, toothache, pain after a tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint pain, neuralgia, back pain, muscle pain, stiff shoulders, bruising pain, fracture pain, sprain pain, menstrual pain (period pain) and pain from injury, and to bring down fever when there are chills (feeling cold and shivering) and a raised temperature.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 11 years and over: take 1 capsule at a time, 1 to 3 times in 1 day, avoiding an empty stomach. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease should use ibuprofen only after careful consideration and should avoid high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg in 1 day). People with cardiovascular risk factors (for example high blood pressure, high blood fats, diabetes, smoking) who need high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg in 1 day) should consider carefully before starting long-term treatment. Clinical studies have shown that high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg in 1 day) may slightly increase the risk of arterial thrombotic events (myocardial infarction or stroke).

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you have had asthma with this medicine or with another antipyretic analgesic or cold medicine, or if the user is an infant under 3 months of age.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, thyroid disease, diabetes or high blood pressure; if you are physically weak, have a high fever or are an older person; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain or another stomach problem that lasts or comes back, or an ulcer or a bleeding problem; if you have lost a lot of body fluid through vomiting and diarrhoea or are unable to take fluid in; or if the user is a child under 2 years of age.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 or 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it together with other antipyretic analgesics, cold medicines or sedatives.
Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with diuretics, low-dose aspirin, or medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants or steroids.

If rash or reddening, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, stomach pain, bleeding from the digestive tract, stomach discomfort, dizziness or oedema occurs, or rarely shock (hives, swelling and tightness of the chest immediately after a dose, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome — severe symptoms with high fever, and a rash or reddening with burn-like blisters, on the skin of the whole body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, or very rarely erythema multiforme, exfoliative dermatitis, a photosensitivity reaction of unknown frequency, drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) or acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Ointment (A77202COM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for haemorrhoids.
groups.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area 2 times in 1 day, as far as possible after a bowel movement.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it. To prevent the problem coming back, go on applying it over a long period even after symptoms such as inflammation, itching, blisters and a burning feeling have gone. Use this medicine only around the anus, and do not use it for the eyes.

Mild itching, pain and bleeding may occur.
